title: Product of Array Except Self
oneLinerQuestion: Construct an output array where each index equals the product of all array elements except itself.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Product of Array Except Self problem requires calculating an output array such that each element at index i equals the product of all numbers in the original array except nums[i], strictly without using the division operator and in O(N) time. The product of all numbers except nums[i] can be broken down into two distinct sub-products: the product of all elements to the left of index i (prefix product) and the product of all elements to the right of index i (postfix product). By first calculating the prefix products across a forward pass directly into the output array, and then multiplying each element by a running postfix product across a backward pass, we achieve optimal O(N) time while using O(1) auxiliary space (excluding the output array itself).

- Step 1: Output Array Allocation & State Initialization — We allocate an output array `res = new Array(nums.length)` and initialize a running prefix tracker `prefix = 1`.

- Step 2: Forward Pass (Prefix Accumulation) — We iterate through `nums` from left to right (`i = 0` to `nums.length - 1`). At each index, we store the accumulated product of all elements strictly preceding it: `res[i] = prefix`. We then incorporate the current element into the prefix tracker: `prefix *= nums[i]`.

- Step 3: Postfix Tracker Setup — We initialize a running postfix tracker `postfix = 1` to accumulate products coming from the right boundary of the array.

- Step 4: Backward Pass (Postfix Multiplication) — We iterate through `nums` in reverse order (`i = nums.length - 1` down to `0`). At each index, we multiply the existing prefix product already stored in `res[i]` by the running postfix product: `res[i] *= postfix`. We then update the running postfix product to include the current element: `postfix *= nums[i]`.

- Step 5: Termination & Output Delivery — Once the reverse pass completes, every position `res[i]` holds the exact product of all prefix elements multiplied by all postfix elements, satisfying the condition without performing division. We return `res`.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N) where N is the length of `nums`, as the algorithm consists of two sequential linear passes. Space Complexity: O(1) auxiliary space beyond the returned output array, as only two scalar variables (`prefix` and `postfix`) are maintained.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION productExceptSelf(nums):
    res = ARRAY_OF_SIZE(LENGTH(nums), INITIAL_VALUE = 1)
    prefix = 1
    FOR i FROM 0 TO LENGTH(nums) - 1 DO:
        res[i] = prefix; prefix = prefix * nums[i]
    END FOR
    postfix = 1
    FOR i FROM LENGTH(nums) - 1 DOWN TO 0 DO:
        res[i] = res[i] * postfix; postfix = postfix * nums[i]
    END FOR
    RETURN res
END FUNCTION
